key_insight: A Coherent Ising Machine–based Bayesian inversion framework targets faster plasma parameter estimation for tokamak control.
engineering_relevance: Faster fusion of tokamak diagnostic data could support real-time plasma control as hardware capacity scales.
method: Formulate plasma parameter inversion as Bayesian maximum a posteriori estimation.
Map the negative log-posterior objective to a spin Hamiltonian for a coupled optical-oscillator CIM.
Use block coordinate descent to accommodate current hardware capacity limits.
evidence_signal: Evaluation on EAST tokamak plasma current profile inversion reports an approximately 1 ms single-run solution time, not end-to-end real-time execution.
watch_item: Current hardware capacity requires block-wise iteration, which still prevents full real-time operation.
paper_title: Solving Large-Scale Parameter Inference in Controllable Nuclear Fusion via Coherent Ising Machines and Block Coordinate Descent
